# Contextual lexical diagnostics

The two parse/ originals are unchanged pinned upstream fixtures. Their old public
lexical ParseError remains unchanged. Optional diagnostic parsing retains a bounded
prefix and uses the actual grammar to select the expected token; no rejected source
becomes an accepted book. The 22 exact cases include earlier grammar errors,
expression/name/declaration contexts, imports, EOF/CRLF and decimal suffixes.

Extra presentation work is capped at 64 source tokens including the fault and
4,096 scanned prefix bytes including trivia (excluding consumed import headers).
The failed loader may construct temporary declarations and binder IDs. It stops
before templates, substitution, foreign path inspection, pre-existing law types,
or nontrivial lowering. Unsupported prefixes retain their original diagnostic.
This cap does not change accepted input or existing parser/evaluator budgets.

Four Unicode controls in the preceding malformed-literal fixture set remain
unqualified. Historical receipts retain their original commit identities. The new
unit tests cover caps, default parser guards, shared template identity, exact
barrier outcomes and public errors. No runtime execution is claimed for refusals.
